content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to this kind of programming and I have a question. I have an irrigation system that moves slowly between two sensors. How can I create a preset counter to select how many times the system moves between the sensors? I would like to use a pushbutton to set the number of cycles.
You can use two or more counters, each with its own preset value, and then select them using an input signal. I've attached the basic start of the program.

I understand, but that approach would require a separate input for each counter. What I’m looking for is a way to use only one input to adjust the cycle count, similar to setting an "on threshold" in the counter using just a pushbutton. For example, pressing the button three times would set the cycle count to three, or eight presses would set it to eight.
Apologies, there was a small error. Here’s a better version.
Hi [user_name], thank you for your assistance. That was exactly what I needed, and it works perfectly in my program. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user was seeking a method to configure a preset counter for controlling the number of movements of a system between two sensors, ideally with just one pushbutton to set the number of cycles. The feedback indicates that such beginner-friendly features or documentation are not straightforward, and flexible input methods are necessary. With community support, the user was able to implement the solution successfully and was satisfied with the result.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a simple way to set the number of repetitions dynamically using just one pushbutton, without needing multiple inputs.
